Maria: heads-up — nightly smokebench shows a p99 regression after the kernel-selector heuristic change. attaching quick dump from the run.

Maria: ```
$ ./bench_harness --scenario=attn_kernels --runs=1000 --note=nightly-heuristic-v2
p50: 12.3ms
p95: 48.1ms
p99: 132.5ms  <- baseline 101.2ms (yesterday)
throughput: 420/s
config: kernel_selector=heuristic_v2 evict_policy=aggressive seq_cutoff=1024
```

Alex: is that spike uniform or concentrated at high seq lengths?

Maria: concentrated at seq>1024. small increase at 512 but negligible. single-GPU a100x2 job.

Jamal: my first guess: kernel switch is causing KV-cache thrashing + evictions mid-inference. heuristic_v2 flips kernel per-layer more aggressively. saw similar pattern in earlier quant experiment.

Eva: can you paste a perf log snippet showing eviction counters? that'd help confirm.

Maria: pasted sample from the runtime logs below. (trimmed)

Maria: ```
[2026-03-20T03:12:45Z] req=0x7f2 evict: freed 24 pages, kv_hits=120 kv_misses=9
[2026-03-20T03:12:45Z] req=0x7f2 switch_kernel: from=fused_attn_v1 to=multi_kern_v2 seq=1536
[2026-03-20T03:12:45Z] req=0x7f2 evict: freed 30 pages, kv_hits=23 kv_misses=15
[2026-03-20T03:12:45Z] latency_us: 128400
```

Jamal: that looks like eviction spikes aligned with kernel switches. eviction frees then immediate cache misses are pushing latency way up.

Alex: can we reproduce in a focused microbench (single request type) and bisect the selector? need to know whether it's the selector logic or new kernels interacting poorly.

Eva: I'll run a microbench job with: `--no-evict` and `--disable-kernel-switch` to isolate. if p99 drops then the switch is the culprit.

ci-bot: scheduled microbench job 1945010800 (microbench/evict-test) queued on a100x1. link: https://ci.internal/runs/1945010800

Maria: result from microbench (short):

Maria: ```
baseline (heuristic_v1): p99=102.3ms
heuristic_v2 w/evict: p99=135.8ms
heuristic_v2 no-evict: p99=108.2ms
heuristic_v2 disable-switch: p99=103.1ms
```

Jamal: that pretty much nails it. eviction + switching together cause the tail. two hypotheses: (1) eviction policy is too aggressive when switch happens, or (2) switching path doesn't warm KV cache properly before compute.

Alex: short-term mitigation: flip flag back to heuristic_v1 for stable channel, and gate heuristic_v2 behind an opt-in runtime flag for canary pools.

ops-bot: rollback flag patch r/9998 deployed to hosted-stable at 1945012400 by ops. (reacted :white_check_mark:)

Eva: follow-ups we should do:
- add a regression test to bench harness that runs mixed-seq requests with kernel-switch enabled and checks p99 delta threshold.
- add an assertion in runtime that logs kv-warmup time when switch happens.
- add eviction counters to telemetry dashboards.

Jamal: I'll add eviction counters + a histogram of kv_warmup_latency in the runtime. assigning myself.

Maria: I'll open a small RFC follow-up for selector heuristics: propose a hysteresis window (don't switch if last switch < N ms) and explicit kv-warmup phase. linking perf numbers.

Alex: can we also add a smoke check to the nightly that fails the run if p99 increases > 15% vs baseline? prevents silent regressions.

Eva: yes — I'll add a threshold check and annotate the run with the selector variant.

Maria: created ticket RW-kernelevict-231 (RFC follow-up + perf checklist).

Jamal: created PR #1245 to emit eviction counters and kv_warmup histogram. review ping @Alex.

Alex: will review today.

Maria: action items recap: rollback done, jamal instrument eviction, eva add bench regression check, maria file RFC. we'll reconvene once PR and RF C posted. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder — if anyone needs capacity to reproduce at scale, file infra-ops ticket with label `perf-critical`.

Eva: thanks all. I'll post microbench logs and the new threshold patch once it's up.

Maria: closing loop for now — good catch by nightly. (reacted :eyes:)
